Crop shows another place of the page (4)

MS 1936 (RASAM-2): the PAGE-XML polygon outlines the right line (page view), but the published crop was cut elsewhere: other lines, the library stamp, or bare paper. 103 of the 250 MS 1936 crops are like this (plus 80 empty ones); only 3 of its 22 test crops are right. So MS 1936's very high error rate is mostly broken crops, not only its Berber text.

What to do: Re-cut from the PAGE-XML polygon; the crop-check table above lists how many crops are affected per manuscript.

Crop contains neighbouring lines (3)

MS 609 (RASAM-1) polygons are generous and the script has tall ascenders and long descenders, so many crops hold large parts of the lines above and below. The model has to guess which line is meant.

What to do: Tighter crops (polygon mask, or baseline-centred band) for training; report these lines separately.

Reference is garbled (uncorrected HTR) (8)

The reference is not sensible Arabic, while both models read fluent, correct text. These cluster on whole pages (MS 1977 pages 0071 and 0158; TariMa RES_MON_8_5560 page 0169), which fits pages that were pre-transcribed by HTR and never proofread.

What to do: Re-transcribe the affected pages (needs someone who reads Maghrebi script); until then drop them from training and report them separately.
